heard: Shortly before 10 a.m., New York's tallest skyscraper vanished into fog. Colonel William Smith steered his B-25 bomber toward Midtown Manhattan. Flying at 200 miles per hour, the plane struck the 79th floor. One engine plummeted down a shaft, severing the heavy elevator cables. Rescuers placed injured operator Betty Lou Oliver into a car to evacuate her. The cables snapped, plunging her 75 stories into the sub-basement. A cushion of trapped air saved her life from the impossible fall. She survived the morning the tallest skyscraper vanished into fog.
